summary: The four supplied false-positive fixtures pass and the JSON envelope is sound, but the repair creates two reproducible false-negative classes: unknown numeric axes are treated as proven unrelated, and any typed object or array that merely mentions every contribution is treated as a registry door.

findings.title: Unknown numeric axes suppress real same-domain drift
evidence: tooling/src/ast/ops/registry-candidates.ts:284-290 derives an axis only from a declared type symbol; primitive number has no declaration and therefore yields undefined.
tooling/src/ast/ops/registry-candidates.ts:293-299 assigns that unresolved value to Record's key axis.
tooling/src/ast/ops/registry-candidates.ts:361-362 classifies numeric overlap as unrelated whenever left.axis is undefined, rather than requiring two resolved, unequal axes.

reproducer.expected: one registry-candidate:drifted-twins finding because both tables explicitly share the number key domain and disagree on one member

findings.testGap: tests/tooling/ast/ops/registry-candidates.test.ts:97-104 calls two Record<string, string> tables unrelated even though both axes are unresolved primitive string. It proves the unsafe unknown-axis suppression but has no same-unknown-axis counter-control.
findings.positiveControl: Two Record<Axis, string> tables importing the same declared Axis alias produced one drifted-twins finding, while separately declared Migration and Position aliases produced none. The resolved-axis branch works; the unknown-axis branch is the defect.

findings.title: Typed-composition recognition suppresses diagnostics that are not registration doors
evidence: tooling/src/ast/ops/registry-candidates.ts:168-183 accepts every typed or satisfies object/array literal and checks only whether descendant identifiers resolve to all sibling declarations.
tooling/src/ast/ops/registry-candidates.ts:89-93 suppresses the entire contribution group when that broad predicate succeeds.
The shared origin helpers resolve the imported identifiers correctly; the overreach is the absence of any requirement that the contributions themselves be values in a registry composition.

reproducer.contributions: three sibling exported objects a, b, and c with fields id, label, render
reproducer.consumer: const DIAGNOSTIC: { allDistinct: boolean } = { allDistinct: a.id !== b.id && b.id !== c.id };
reproducer.expected: one registry-candidate:contribution-without-door finding because the typed value only computes a diagnostic and registers none of the contributions
reproducer.control: Removing only the DIAGNOSTIC type annotation restored the finding, reported as aggregation=hand-maintained at diagnostics.ts.

findings.testGap: tests/tooling/ast/ops/registry-candidates.test.ts:106-117 covers a real readonly Card[] composition but has no typed non-composition control.

intendedFalsePositiveFamilies.evidence: focused test at tests/tooling/ast/ops/registry-candidates.test.ts:73-85 passed; receiver identities are rooted by declaration and static path at registry-candidates.ts:188-223

intendedFalsePositiveFamilies.family: quoted Record keys vs switch literals
intendedFalsePositiveFamilies.evidence: focused test at tests/tooling/ast/ops/registry-candidates.test.ts:87-95 passed; string names normalize through getLiteralText at registry-candidates.ts:43-55
the supplied fixture and an independent resolved-distinct-axis probe suppress the intended false positive, but unknown axes also suppress a real same-domain positive as Finding 1 documents
the readonly Card[] fixture passes, but the predicate also treats typed diagnostics as registration doors as Finding 2 documents

retainedTruePositives: The focused nine-test file passed and its first fixture retained all four candidate kinds.
The imported shared-registry alias fixture retained one shared-namespace-mutation finding.
An independent string-key Record drift probe produced one drifted-twins finding.
An independent same resolved Axis numeric probe produced one drifted-twins finding.
